slides.teacher_cue: New digraph — wh. In standard English, wh makes the same /w/ sound as the letter w. Two letters, one sound — /w/. when, where, while, wheel, white, whale. Important note: 'where', 'while', 'white', 'whale', 'wheat' are now fully decodable because wh = /w/ and the rest of each word uses taught patterns.
slides.expected_response: Students produce /w/ from wh and understand that wh is a digraph making /w/.
slides.correction_move: Show w and wh side by side — same sound, different spelling. Students blend wh-words using the known /w/ onset. Unlock: where = wh+er+e (CVCe), while = wh+i+l+e, white = wh+i+t+e.
slides.observation_note: Watch for students expecting wh to make a new or different sound. Redirect — same /w/ as in win, wet.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the new focus, then connect wh to one strong word from today.

slides.correction_move: Model the focus once, then have students echo and use it in a known word.
slides.observation_note: Listen for whether students can carry the focus from isolation into a real word.
